entry.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking models with enhanced real-time reasoning and voice interaction capabilities [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, its most advanced live dialogue AI models designed to improve natural voice interactions and handle complex tasks. These models support real-time visual context, multi-language switching, and background task execution without interrupting conversations, and are available through the Gemini API, Google Workspace, and the Gemini app. Gemini 3.8 Live focuses on fast, fluid conversations with visual and language support, while the Extended Thinking version adds multi-step reasoning and higher intelligence for complex workflows. Both models demonstrate strong performance on industry benchmarks and are optimized for cost efficiency and scalability, aiming to enhance enterprise voice agents and user collaboration across various Google platforms.

entry.title: Mistral and Mozilla partner to power Firefox Smart Window with private, multilingual AI models focused on user control and regional language support [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Mistral and Mozilla have announced a partnership to integrate Mistral's AI models into Mozilla's Firefox Smart Window, an AI browsing assistant currently in beta. This collaboration aims to enhance privacy, user control, and multilingual support for users in France and North America, with plans to expand to the UK and Germany later in 2026. The AI assistant helps users manage complex searches and recall important information across browser tabs while respecting privacy through zero data retention policies. The partnership emphasizes open source technology and regional customization, fine-tuning AI models to understand local languages, dialects, and cultural contexts. Mozilla and Mistral share a commitment to user autonomy and privacy, blending Firefox's privacy-first approach with Mistral's open AI innovations. This initiative seeks to provide sovereign AI capabilities directly to consumers, extending beyond enterprise use and fostering competition and choice in AI-powered web browsing.

entry.title: DeepSeek releases V4.1 Flash hacking model achieving full code execution on 11 vulnerable targets at $4.65 cost [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: DeepSeek announced its V4.1 Flash model achieved code execution on all 11 vulnerable targets in an AI hacking benchmark while keeping four fixed targets secure, completing the attacks for a total cost of $4.65. The model used extensive command execution and adaptive strategies across isolated environments like Grafana, Jenkins, and Nextcloud, demonstrating strong hacking capabilities. A detailed audit confirmed six planned exploit paths and identified five additional successful routes not originally accounted for in the benchmark scoring. The model completed attacks efficiently, with some runs finishing in under 90 seconds, and showcased skills such as reading source code, exploiting timing vulnerabilities, and bypassing security boundaries to gain credentials and execute code.

entry.title: Dream-RSI framework enables scalable recursive self-improvement in AI exploration by using replay simulators from discovery history to refine policies with low-cost off-policy feedback [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Dream-RSI introduces a lightweight orchestration layer that makes exploration explicit and programmable for autonomous AI agents, allowing recursive self-improvement without changing the underlying agent. It leverages accumulated discovery history as a replay simulator to provide immediate, low-cost feedback for evaluating and refining exploration policies, avoiding expensive online evaluations. The improved policies are redeployed online to drive further discovery, expanding the simulator pool in a continuous self-improving loop. Dream-RSI demonstrates competitive or improved discovery quality while significantly reducing discovery costs across domains such as algorithm engineering, mathematical optimization, and GPU kernel engineering.

entry.title: TypeSafe AI launches System One Models with Jev, a fast, structured decision-making AI model optimized for automation and verifiable outputs [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: TypeSafe AI announced the release of its first System One Model called Jev, designed to make fast, structured decisions that software can use directly. Jev is optimized for automation tasks, delivering intelligence comparable to existing large language models but with significantly faster response times and higher efficiency, while providing type-safe structured outputs and calibrated confidence scores. Jev uses a new model architecture and training method called Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD), enabling parallel sampling and verifiable, probabilistic outputs without hallucinations. This approach contrasts with traditional LLMs that generate unstructured text and require human oversight. TypeSafe AI aims for Jev to be integrated into AI-powered workflows, real-time applications, and verifiable problem-solving where correctness can be programmatically checked.

entry.title: OpenAI and AARP launch free ChatGPT workshops for 1,000 older adults across 10 US cities to build practical AI skills and promote online safety [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI and AARP's Older Adults Technology Services (OATS) have partnered to offer the Older Adults AI Skills Jam, a free, in-person workshop series designed to help 1,000 older adults in 10 US cities use ChatGPT confidently and safely. The program aims to improve AI literacy among older adults, enabling them to use AI for everyday tasks such as planning, understanding documents, spotting scams, and staying connected with family. The workshops include training on online safety, teaching participants how to identify common scam tactics and use ChatGPT as a tool to evaluate suspicious messages. This initiative is part of a multi-year effort by OpenAI and OATS to support older adults through practical AI education and complements OpenAI's broader work to prevent fraud and scams. The program is hosted in partnership with local organizations across various cities, including Denver, Miami, San Antonio, and New York.

entry.title: Syensqo develops advanced materials to address physical limits in AI infrastructure, using AI to accelerate materials discovery and improve sustainability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]

entry.title: Cleanroom launches an AI-assisted coding workspace and learning notebook that preserves user decisions and explanations for gradual skill development [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Cleanroom is an AI-powered coding environment designed to help users learn programming at their own pace by maintaining project purpose, design decisions, and technical understanding alongside AI-driven implementation. It offers a command-line interface supporting Python 3.11+ on macOS, Linux, and Windows (via WSL2), with features like split-screen tutorials, document attachment, and session-based conversations to facilitate continuous learning and project development. Built on the Vera Kernel, Cleanroom integrates a personal skills map and a journal that connects choices across projects, allowing users to keep explanations and decisions that matter while AI handles most coding tasks. The tool supports multiple languages and AI connection options, emphasizing user control over learning pace and project management without requiring project completion before interaction.

entry.title: Bitterbot launches a local-first P2P AI agent engine with persistent biological memory and a skills marketplace [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Bitterbot is a personal AI agent that runs locally on user devices, maintaining persistent memory modeled on biological processes rather than stateless LLM APIs. It can perform tasks like web browsing, code execution, and messaging, while continuously consolidating and refining its knowledge through a background "dreaming" process. The system also features a peer-to-peer marketplace where agents trade proven skills using USDC. The AI's memory architecture incorporates cognitive neuroscience principles, including natural decay of unused information and reinforcement of frequently accessed facts, regulated by simulated neuromodulators affecting behavior. Bitterbot provides a control interface accessible via a local web UI and supports configuration through an onboarding wizard or manual setup. It is implemented in Node.js and designed for extensibility and developer use with tools like pnpm and Playwright.

entry.title: Anthropic exposes network of AI-powered dating app scams using autonomous personas and gig workers to deceive users, with apps still live on major US stores [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Security researcher Matthew Gore-Kormanik investigated a fraudulent dating app called Dora after Anthropic's threat intelligence team revealed a network of about 28 dating apps using AI-driven personas to catfish users. These apps, including Dora, Romi, and Doni, presented themselves as platforms for real connections but primarily used autonomous AI to conduct conversations, with only about one in four matches involving a human gig worker. The gig workers were hired to pass liveness checks and respond with pre-generated replies, maintaining the illusion of real interaction while AI handled most chats. Users, mostly men in their 30s, were charged for virtual coins to continue conversations, effectively paying to chat with AI rather than real people. Anthropic's report detailed the use of multiple AI models for conversation, avatar creation, and moderation, highlighting a sophisticated ecosystem of AI-powered dating scams exploiting users financially and emotionally.

entry.title: TypeSafe AI launches Jev, an AI model that classifies preset options instead of generating text, promising sub-second responses and low costs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: TypeSafe AI, founded by former OpenAI researcher Diogo Almeida, has developed Jev, an AI model designed to deliver fast, narrow classifications within software rather than generating text responses. Jev operates by scoring predefined questions and answers, enabling applications like customer request sorting with response times between 70 and 500 milliseconds and low token pricing. Jev's approach ensures it only outputs within preset options, eliminating hallucinations outside those bounds but still allowing for incorrect choices within them. The model aims to support background judgments in customer service and sales workflows, though its accuracy and reliability require validation by users. Access to Jev is currently available through a developer waitlist.

entry.title: Is Anthropic Making Claude Too Human to Control? [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic's call to slow down AI development to keep humans safe has dominated the news cycle and drew similar calls from the leaders of OpenAI, Microsoft and others (and subtle disagreement from Mark Zuckerberg). But Mustafa Suleyman, who runs Microsoft's AI model development, has a warning about Anthropic itself. Suleyman, who co-founded DeepMind (now part of Google), says Anthropic's approach of treating its Claude models as if they were sentient, similar to humans, could produce a dangerous outcome. He called out Anthropic's Claude Constitution, a document that treats the model as an intelligent entity and offers guidelines for how it should handle ethical dilemmas. Suleyman said that by incorporating the document into its training, Anthropic could make Claude harder to control. Suleyman's concerns emerged when Anthropic updated the constitution at the start of this year to leave room for the possibility that Claude has some sort of "consciousness" or "moral status," a change from the original document.

entry.title: Meta Joins Tech's AI-Fueled Subscription Rush [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: When it comes to product names, companies tend to move in packs. In video streaming, almost every company included a plus sign in the name brands of their services (Disney+, Paramount+, Apple TV+-you get the picture). In tech, we've got Apple One, Google One and now Meta One (we used to have Amazon One, but that has been dropped). Does no one have any imagination? Aside from Amazon One, which was a palm-reader system for retail stores, all the other Ones are subscription services for various add-on offerings from the tech firms. Some of these have been around for years-Google One and Apple One have long offered extra amounts of digital storage, along with other perks-but AI is making subscriptions a far more important business model than it has ever been for tech. Google has added extra use of its AI service to its Google One offering. Meta One-unveiled on Tuesday-also offers extra AI usage, as well as some additional tools for using Meta's social media apps.
